title: In everything give thanks (1 Thessalonians 5:18)

cards: "Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks." Three short lines near the end of Paul's first letter to the Thessalonians. On a coffee mug they'd look cheerful, almost easy.
Then read the letter around them. Paul says this church received the word "in much affliction." He writes to comfort them about friends who have died, those he calls "them which are asleep."
These are people in trouble and in grief. And to them, not to people having a good week, he writes: in every thing, give thanks.

teach.b: The King James reads: "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you." In every thing. Some readers lean hard on that little word.
On their reading, Paul doesn't ask the grieving to be thankful that their friends died. He asks them to find thanks inside whatever is happening.

Other readers point to Ephesians, which says "giving thanks always for all things," and hold the two lines together. Either way, the thanks doesn't wait for the trouble to clear. Paul seems to have practiced it himself.

teach.h: I HAVE LEARNED TO BE CONTENT.
teach.b: Writing to the Philippians while in bonds, he says: "I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content." Learned. Something practiced, not something he was born with.
And there's an older pattern behind him.
Psalm 136 repeats one refrain, line after line: "for his mercy endureth for ever." Thanks as a rhythm, said again and again until it sinks in. One more example.

teach.h: HE TOOK BREAD, AND GAVE THANKS.
teach.b: On the night Jesus was betrayed, Luke says, "he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it." Thanks, at that table, on that night. Christians build this into ordinary days.
A grace said before a meal. A few minutes at bedtime looking back for the day's gifts. A line of thanks at the start of prayer, before any asking.
Not a feeling summoned on command. A habit of looking.

how: Christians practice gratitude through grace before meals, thanksgiving at the start of prayer, and some through a nightly review of the day's gifts; churches give thanks in worship together, and some keep special days of thanksgiving.

games.q: what does “in everything give thanks” mean?
o: a grace said aloud before every family meal
thanking God only once the trouble has passed
finding thanks inside every situation, even hard days

games.q: in everything, thanks — tap the pairs.
p: I have learned to be content
he took bread, and gave thanks

s: Paul wrote "in every thing give thanks" to a church having an easy time
the letter speaks of "much affliction" and comforts them about friends who had died.
the King James line says "in every thing," not "for every thing"
"in every thing give thanks." some readers find that small word matters; Ephesians adds "for all things."
Jesus gave thanks over bread on the night he was betrayed
Luke: "he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it."

games.q: you're in the church at Thessalonica. you've buried friends and faced trouble. a letter from Paul is read aloud. what does it ask of you?
o: wait until things get better, then give thanks.
give thanks only for the good parts, and ignore the rest.
games.why: "rejoice evermore. pray without ceasing. in every thing give thanks." written to people in grief, not to people having a good week.

practice: Count ten gifts on your fingers, small and specific: not my family, but the way your sister laughed on the phone; not health, but the knee that worked on the stairs this morning.
If the day has been hard, look inside it anyway, the way Paul asked, and if you pray, say thanks for each one.
If grief feels too heavy to carry alone, or you're thinking of harming yourself, please call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: In everything give thanks. Paul's line to a grieving church: thanks found inside every situation, not saved for the good days.

orig.note: Greek, 1 Thessalonians 5:18: give thanks — a command, addressed to the whole church.

carryVoice: Your line: in everything, thanks. The thanks doesn't wait for the trouble to clear. Until tomorrow.
